correctness.rationale: The recurrence closed form implies the tail generator identity. The exchange argument proves optimal change for {1,c,d}, and the exact shift-count inequality proves Apéry minimality; its maximum and sum determine F and genus. Explicit maximal-residue analysis gives exactly two PF gaps. A separate shortest-path enumerator verified complete Apéry rows and invariants for all b from 2 through 17; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The infinite shifted Jacobsthal recurrence is a natural extension of studied shifted Fibonacci and generalized Jacobsthal Frobenius problems. A complete symbolic Apéry set determines all gaps, F and genus, and an unexpectedly uniform type-two pseudo-Frobenius classification for a four-minimal-generator family; these are intrinsic, motivated semigroup invariants. The shift four is the first natural small case with four minimal generators for b>=3, not an arbitrary finite slice.
